title: When Tukey meets Chauvenet: a new boxplot criterion for outlier detection
summary: The paper addresses the fact that Tukey’s boxplot uses one-size-fits-all fences while Chauvenet’s criterion is not robust to contaminated data. It fuses the two by expressing Tukey’s quartile fences through robust mean/SD estimates and setting the sample-size-adjusted coefficient k_n^Chau = Φ^{-1}(1-0.25/n)/1.35 - 0.5. In normal-data simulations with two contaminated points, the Chauvenet-type boxplot labels 2 total suspected outliers at n=500 (vs 3 for Tukey) and many fewer false positives at larger n, and it detects the 3 junior civil-service pay freezes in the real Hong Kong data.

claims.statement: For standard-normal data with n=500 and two contaminated points 5 and 6, the Chauvenet-type boxplot labels 2 total suspected outliers.
claims.dataset: Simulated N(0,1) n=500 with two contaminated points 5 and 6
claims.config_for_value: R set.seed(1863); draw first 498 observations from N(0,1), append 5 and 6; use Chauvenet-type fences with k^Chau_n = qnorm(1-0.25/500)/1.35 - 0.5; count observations outside LF/UF.
claims.quote: it labels a total of 2, 2, 2 and 3 suspected outliers for the simulated data with 4 different sample sizes, respectively.

match_target.why: This is the cheapest central demonstration: one sub-second R simulation at n=500 directly tests the new Chauvenet-type coefficient against Tukey’s baseline, matching the user’s target hint without needing larger-n or real-data work.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: no std is reported for the target count, and it is not an accuracy/F1/AUC bounded score; 10% relative on value 2 gives 1.8–2.2, which admits only the integer 2.

requirements.stmt: Compute the normal-data fence coefficient as k_n^Chau = qnorm(1 - 0.25/n)/1.35 - 0.5.
requirements.quote: This leads to 1.35kn + 0.675 = Φ−1(1 −0.25/n), or equivalently, kn = Φ−1(1 −0.25/n)/1.35 −0.5.

requirements.stmt: Form the normal-data Chauvenet-type lower and upper fences as Q1 - k*IQR and Q3 + k*IQR.
requirements.quote: By formula (1), recall that the lower and upper fences in Tukey’s boxplot are LFn = Q1−kn×IQR and UFn = Q3 + kn×IQR.

requirements.stmt: Use IQR = Q3 - Q1 from the sample quartiles.
requirements.quote: by letting IQR = Q3 −Q1 be the interquartile range of the data

requirements.stmt: Use Tukey’s baseline inner fences with k = 1.5.
requirements.quote: Tukey (1977) further referred to the fences with k = 1.5 as the “inner fences”, and with k = 3 as the “outer fences”.

requirements.stmt: Label an observation as a suspected outlier when it lies strictly outside either fence.
requirements.quote: if an observation X is either smaller than LFn or larger than UFn, then it will be labeled as an α-outlier in the boxplot.

requirements.stmt: For the normal simulation, draw the first n-2 observations from the standard normal distribution.
requirements.quote: we generate the first n −2 observations as a random sample from the standard normal distribution

requirements.stmt: Append the two contaminated points X_{n-1}=5 and X_n=6.
requirements.quote: designate the last two observations as contaminated data with Xn−1 = 5 and Xn = 6.

requirements.stmt: Use set.seed(1863) before generating the normal sample.
requirements.quote: with set.seed(1863) in R, Tukey’s boxplot will label a total of 3, 48 and 357 suspected outliers

requirements.stmt: Report the total number of suspected outliers, not only false positives after removing the two known contaminated points.
requirements.quote: it labels a total of 2, 2, 2 and 3 suspected outliers for the simulated data with 4 different sample sizes, respectively.

requirements.stmt: Compute Q1 and Q3 as the sample first and third quartiles.
requirements.quote: Let also Q1 and Q3 be the first and third quartiles of the data, respectively.

data.name: Simulated standard normal with two contaminated points
data.how_to_get: In R: set.seed(1863); x <- c(rnorm(498, 0, 1), 5, 6); n <- length(x) = 500. This is the normal-data simulation in Section 4.1.

data.name: Hong Kong civil service pay adjustment data
data.how_to_get: Download annual pay-adjustment tables from https://www.csb.gov.hk/english/admin/pay/55.html; Table 1 lists the 18 years since 2007 used for junior and senior groups.
